facts: Source of fresh, local tropical fruits

items.description: Sarchí is Costa Rica's most famous artisan town, renowned for its colorful and intricately painted wooden oxcarts.
The art of making corn tortillas by hand on a clay comal is a cherished culinary tradition inherited from indigenous cultures.
facts: Made from ground masa and water
Often cooked over traditional wood fires

items.description: Exquisite hand-carved masks created by the Boruca people, traditionally used in the annual 'Dance of the Devils' festival.
facts: Carved from balsa or cedar wood

items.description: Gallo Pinto is the quintessential Costa Rican breakfast, a flavorful mixture of seasoned rice and black beans.
facts: Served with eggs, cheese, and plantains

items.description: The carving of lightweight balsa wood into intricate animal and bird figurines is a specialized craft found in rural regions.
A spectacular Afro-Caribbean festival in Puerto Limón, celebrating the region's unique cultural heritage with parades and music.
Traditional Chorotega pottery uses ancient pre-Columbian techniques and natural pigments to create beautiful ceramic art.
facts: Based in Guaitil and San Vicente

items.description: Pineapple production is a major pillar of the agricultural economy, with Costa Rica being a top global exporter of the fruit.

facts: Daily harvests of fresh local seafood
Strong cultural ties to the ocean
